title: Integrated In Vivo and In Silico Approaches for Targeting JAK2/STAT3/SOCS3: Repurposing Boeravinone B and Resveratrol as Chemopreventive Agents in Colon Cancer.
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦结肠癌中JAK2/STAT3/SOCS3通路的小分子药物重定位，虽含分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Colon cancer ranks among the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and contributes substantially to cancer-related mortality. This study employed an integrated approach to evaluate the chemopreventive effects of Boeravinone B (BB) and Resveratrol (REV), administered individually and in combination, in the azoxymethane (AOM)-induced rat model of colon cancer, with particular emphasis on cytokine signaling pathways and mitochondrial regulation of apoptosis. The combination of BB (15 mg/kg) and REV (8 mg/kg) exhibited greater efficacy than either treatment alone. These combined treatments (BB + REV) significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha [TNF-alpha]), nitro-oxidative stress indicators (NO, iNOS), and histological damage, while promoting mitochondria-mediated apoptosis via modulation of BAX and BCL2. Network analysis revealed that centrality metrics (betweenness, closeness, degree, and stress centrality), identified STAT3, SOCS3, JAK2, BAX, and BCL2 as key hub proteins involved in cytokine signaling and apoptotic pathways. These nodes exhibited the highest centrality values (betweenness: 0.046667 for STAT3/SOCS3/JAK2; degree: 10 for all five proteins), indicating their pivotal roles as therapeutic targets. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities of BB for SOCS3 (-9.0 kcal/mol), BAX (-9.0 kcal/mol), JAK2 (-8.1 kcal/mol), and STAT3 (-7.8 kcal/mol). In comparison, REV exhibited its highest binding affinities for SOCS3 (-7.2 kcal/mol) and BAX (-7.0 kcal/mol). These findings identify SOCS3, BAX, JAK2, and STAT3 as potential molecular targets mediating the combined treatment's anti-inflammatory and pro-apoptotic effects. This integrated in vivo and in silico study showed that combined BB and REV exerted a stronger chemopreventive effect against AOM-induced colon cancer via complementary mechanisms: restoring mitochondrial adenosine triphosphate synthase (ATPase) activity, suppressing biomarkers of inflammation, nitro-oxidative stress, and apoptosis, with strong binding affinities. These findings support repurposing BB and REV as a multitargeted combination therapy against colon cancer.
abstract_zh: 结肠癌在全球最常见的恶性肿瘤中位居前列，并显著导致癌症相关死亡率。本研究采用综合方法评估了Boeravinone B (BB)和Resveratrol (REV)单独及联合给药在氧化偶氮甲烷 (azoxymethane, AOM)诱导的大鼠结肠癌模型中的化学预防效果，特别关注细胞因子信号通路和线粒体凋亡调控。BB（15 mg/kg）和REV（8 mg/kg）的联合用药表现出优于任一单独治疗的疗效。这些联合治疗（BB + REV）显著降低了促炎细胞因子（IL-1beta、IL-6、肿瘤坏死因子-alpha [TNF-alpha]）、硝基氧化应激指标（NO、iNOS）及组织学损伤，同时通过调节BAX和BCL2促进线粒体介导的凋亡。网络分析显示，中心性指标（介数中心性、接近中心性、度中心性和应力中心性）识别出STAT3、SOCS3、JAK2、BAX和BCL2为参与细胞因子信号和凋亡通路的关键枢纽蛋白。这些节点表现出最高的中心性值（介数中心性：STAT3/SOCS3/JAK2为0.046667；度中心性：所有五种蛋白均为10），表明其作为治疗靶点的关键作用。分子对接显示BB对SOCS3（-9.0 kcal/mol）、BAX（-9.0 kcal/mol）、JAK2（-8.1 kcal/mol）和STAT3（-7.8 kcal/mol）具有有利的结合亲和力。相比之下，REV对SOCS3（-7.2 kcal/mol）和BAX（-7.0 kcal/mol）表现出最高的结合亲和力。这些发现将SOCS3、BAX、JAK2和STAT3确定为介导联合治疗抗炎和促凋亡效应的潜在分子靶点。这项综合体内和计算机模拟研究表明，BB和REV联合用药通过互补机制对AOM诱导的结肠癌发挥更强的化学预防作用：恢复线粒体三磷酸腺苷合酶 (adenosine triphosphate synthase, ATPase) 活性，抑制炎症、硝基氧化应激和凋亡的生物标志物，并具有强结合亲和力。这些发现支持将BB和REV重新定位为针对结肠癌的多靶点联合治疗策略。
